resources.string: Tolls: toll button on the map. Motorbike is routed like a car. \"Prefer paved\" takes the alternative with the least unpaved road if it costs under 25 %% more time.
Balanced: a little more time for a shorter route
Takes a clearly shorter alternative (3%%+, no more toll) when it costs at most this much extra time. Off in Emergency. Applies from the next route.
EUR per km of toll road
Balanced mode compares the toll with the time it saves, at the value of the current mode (urgency button).
Adaptive: 30° when slow, up to 50° at motorway speed. North up is flat.
Driving still zooms out with speed. The overview button (while navigating) shows the rest of the route flat, with the places along it; it comes back to this view by itself.
Short: only the maneuver -- \"In 100 m, turn right\", \"Turn right\", \"Take the 3rd exit\" -- no street names, no \"Continue for...\". Applies from the next route.

Instructions, sight tips and the guide\'s Wikipedia readings (in English when a place has no article in your language). Spanish uses a Latin American voice when your phone has one (Android Settings > Text-to-speech). Applies from the next route.
Record my track while navigating (on this phone only)
While Backpack is open, navigation, the speed alarm (by car) and sight tips go on with the screen off or another app in front. Exit stops everything.

The ring fills with your speed: blue, green (top = the limit\'s middle range), yellow near the limit, red over it. 5+ over: blinking with a high beep; 20+ over: the beep without pause. On roads of 100+: blue with a low buzz below 70%% of the limit, red with a low buzz when stopped. Limits come from OpenStreetMap, loaded for the road ahead of your route.

From OpenStreetMap, where mapped (not all are). A sonar blip that speeds up as you get closer. France: only \"Danger zone\" for the stretch, as the law requires. Germany, Switzerland, Cyprus, North Macedonia: silent (warnings are illegal there), and silent when the country is unknown. Mobile checks and traffic are not covered.
Sights are shown in Weekend mode: the small camera next to the Weekend button turns them on or off (hold it for the list).
Places of the kinds at the top are proposed first, even when less famous.
No destination: around the map centre

Places you can reach in this time with the current travel mode from the centre of the map (your position while the map follows you). Your backpack services use the same time. By car the public route service answers up to 1 h; 2 h uses a distance estimate.
Sights along the proposed routes that you can visit within this extra time.
Tell me when a sight is coming up (voice + message)

Time, not distance: worked out with your route\'s average speed, so it fits walking, cycling and driving. Said once per place, never close to a turn. Tap the message to hear what Wikipedia says about it, or to add it as a stop.
An alternative passing clearly more sights is taken if it is at most this much slower.
Backpack services along a route: longest detour

With a destination: the services you ticked in the backpack, along the route within this detour (Weekend mode: the detour in Settings > Sights). Emergency adds hospitals, police and fire stations (15 min) and hides sights. Without a destination: within the reach time (Settings > Sights) of the map centre; Emergency always around you.
Places are fetched per square of about 5 km and kept on this phone (everyday places 3 days, sights 2 weeks), so an area already seen needs no server.
Backpack is free and built on these open projects. If it helps you, consider supporting them.
Map data, places, speed limits and addresses. © OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL).
The map tiles you see. © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
The map engine drawing the map on your phone (BSD licence).
Routes, reroutes, reach areas and second places source.
Searches the OpenStreetMap data for places, sights and speed limits.
Address search while you type (Nominatim by the OpenStreetMap Foundation as fallback).
Which places are well known, and the articles to read about them (Wikidata CC0, Wikipedia CC BY-SA).
Button icons (Go, Stop, Cancel, Resume, sound, sights, tolls). Apache License 2.0.
Sunset: night map from sunset to sunrise where you are. Night always uses the dark map.
OpenFreeMap and VersaTiles: free, no account, no key. VersaTiles (Colorful, Graybeard, Eclipse) has no uptime guarantee.

No account, no tracking. Servers only get what they need: the trip\'s points (routing), ~5 km squares (places), the road ahead (speed limits). Searches are rounded to ~1 km. Recorded trips stay on this phone.
Optional. Backpack works without any of this.
Routes come from openrouteservice (HeiGIT, non-profit). Your own free key keeps your routes on your own account, with your own daily quota. Your own server: its address, without /v2.
. The key stays on this phone and only goes to that server. Order: that server, your own, then the free overpass-api.de and overpass.private.coffee; a slow one gets help from the next.
Style URL (day map; empty = Map page)
Any MapLibre style.json (e.g. from your own tile server). Used by day; the night style stays the one chosen on the Map page.

Routes come from openrouteservice, a free non-profit service (HeiGIT, Heidelberg). Each person uses their own free key: your routes stay on your own account, with your own daily quota. Map, places, sights and the speed alarm work without it.
1. Get my free key: create the account (email + confirmation).\n2. Create a key (token) there and press its copy button.\n3. Come back to Backpack: the key is found and checked by itself.
That doesn\'t look like a key (no spaces, quite long).
Key found on the clipboard, checking…
✓ Key works, saved. You can plan routes now.
openrouteservice refused this key. Copy it again from your account (the whole key).
Saved, but it couldn\'t be checked now (no connection?). It will be used for the next route.
